findings.evidence: At 25% it is still on the board with a shadow. At 50% it hangs over the grass on its side, and at 75% it stands upright on its stem in the air, well above the lawn, with no shadow under it. spin_top in physics/top.jl solves 'on a plane at z = 0', and the frames are only played back at the board's height.
findings.suggestion: Give the solver the board as a finite disc (or the island's ground height under the contact point) so a top that rolls off falls and lands. Or cut the take before it leaves, and post it as 'a take that misses' instead of a joke caption that admits the bug.
findings.what: The blue top floats in mid-air above the grass, past the board's edge, for over half the film. It stands upright on its stem with no shadow and no contact with anything.
findings.where: two-turned-tops: storyboard frames 5-16; full-size frames at 50% and 75%

findings.evidence: The red top is already tilted and spinning in frame 1, and the blue one first appears in frame 2, already spinning beside it. tops.jl has a wind-and-release interaction (HOLD 1), but the film never shows it.
findings.suggestion: Open on Lumi winding the string and letting go, or on the top coming off the lathe, then follow the spin.
findings.what: The film has no cause: no hand, string or Lumi is ever seen, and both tops are already spinning in the first frame. 'Two tops I turned' never shows the turning (the lathe) or the throw.

findings.evidence: Only wirebench.jl changed this session. Its header describes elastic and then plastic joints, work hardening, springback and fatigue snapping, all simulated, and none of it appears in any post.
findings.suggestion: Film the wire being bent back and forth at one spot until it cracks and snaps. That is new, and it is what this session made.
findings.what: The session's real new work, a copper wire that bends plastically, springs back and snaps from fatigue, has no post. The post that did go up re-shows the previous session's tops.

fun_why: The red top's wobble and precession are pleasant to watch once, but a floating blue top and a fixed low camera with nobody spinning them leave little to come back for.
real_change: Neither session plugin makes what the film shows. wirebench.jl (both copies, 207 lines) adds a copper rod on a board that you bend with keys 2/3/4: physics/wire.jl gives each joint elastic then plastic bending, work hardening, springback and fatigue cracking. No post shows any of it. The tops come from s143's physics/top.jl and tops.jl. physics/top.jl is a real rigid body: mass and inertia from the turned profile, contact at the lowest point of the curved surface, sliding friction. But it is solved against an endless plane at z = 0 and played back on a mesh, so the board and the island's ground never take part in the solve. That is why the blue top 'leaves' the board and keeps spinning in thin air.
real_why: The top dynamics are a real simulation (inertia from the profile, a contact point that moves over the curved surface, friction), but its ground is an imaginary plane, cut off from the world it is drawn in.
summary: A real rigid-body top simulation, but for over half the film the blue top hangs in the air above the grass with no shadow, standing on its stem. The caption calls this a joke instead of a miss. The session's own work, a copper wire bender, has no post at all.
surprise_why: Real tops tilting and precessing because of their turned shape and friction is something the island never showed before, but on film it reads as two toys wobbling on a brown disc.
